basic_info.name: SNOMED CT India (national releases via NRCeS) and the Common Drug Codes for India (CDCI) SNOMED CT national drug extension
basic_info.description: SNOMED CT is the world's most comprehensive multilingual clinical terminology, owned and distributed by SNOMED International (London). India has been a SNOMED International Member since March 2014, and the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare (MoH&FW) designated the National Resource Centre for EHR Standards (NRCeS), hosted at C-DAC Pune, as India's National Release Centre (NRC). Within India, SNOMED CT is made available free of charge, but only through an Affiliate License that every developer, deployer or distributor of a SNOMED-enabled product must hold, obtained by registering at the Member Licensing and Distribution Service (MLDS) and accepting the Affiliate License Agreement; because an Affiliate License grants use, the vendor must sublicense end users and file an annual usage report (Declaration of Use, due by 15 January in MLDS). NRCeS also produces national releases, of which the most relevant to MediKiosk is the Common Drug Codes for India (CDCI), a national drug extension that adds supplier, trade/brand-name, clinical-drug (generic) and real-clinical-drug (branded) concepts to SNOMED CT and is the terminology behind the ABDM medication ValueSet (ndhm-medicine-codes). The single most load-bearing fact for MediKiosk is the licensing chain: SNOMED CT and the CDCI Terminology Integrated Package are free to use within India but only under a valid India Affiliate License plus sublicensing and annual usage reporting, whereas the CDCI Flat Files Package is distributed separately under its own bundled License.txt - so a commercial kiosk product must register on MLDS, sublicense its deployed instances, and report annually, or it is using the terminology without a licence even though the content costs zero rupees.
basic_info.organization: SNOMED International (International Health Terminology Standards Development Organisation, London, UK) owns and licenses SNOMED CT. In India, NRCeS at the Centre for Development of Advanced Computing (C-DAC), Pune, acts as the National Release Centre on behalf of the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare (MoH&FW), publishes national releases (including CDCI, the AYUSH Extension, Common Lab Codes for India and reference sets) and administers India Affiliate Licensing through MLDS. The SNOMED CT AYUSH Extension content is authored by CCRAS, CCRS and CCRUM under the Ministry of AYUSH and maintained by NRCeS.
basic_info.country: India (NRCeS / C-DAC Pune; governing owner SNOMED International is UK-based with global membership). India has been a SNOMED International Member since March 2014.
basic_info.status: production / active. SNOMED CT India licensing, the MLDS portal and NRCeS national releases are live and current: CDCI releases continue at a regular cadence (Flat Files releases dated 15 June 2026 and 31 August 2026), and the national drug content is now also surfaced through the government's Drug Registry launched on 29 June 2026.

technical_features.what_it_does: SNOMED CT provides the concept-based clinical terminology Indian health IT is expected to use, and NRCeS national releases localise it. For a FHIR/ABDM output contract such as Module C's OPConsultRecord, SNOMED CT supplies the coded clinical content: problem/diagnosis concepts, findings, procedures, and the medicine codes carried by the ABDM MedicationRequest and MedicationStatement. The CDCI national extension is the key localisation for prescriptions - because SNOMED CT International carries International Non-proprietary Name generics but not Indian trade/brand names, the CDCI adds supplier, product (trade/brand) name, clinical drug (generic) and real clinical drug (branded) concepts so that an Indian medication line can be coded as SNOMED 373873005 'Pharmaceutical / biologic product' Clinical Drug / Real Clinical Drug. The ABDM Medicine Codes ValueSet (ndhm-medicine-codes, system http://snomed.info/sct) is explicitly populated from SNOMED CT International Edition Clinical Drugs plus CDCI Clinical Drugs and Branded Medicines. In licensing terms the standard's function is gated: the terminology, the CDCI Terminology Integrated Package and the national reference sets are all delivered to Affiliate Licensees through MLDS, so software that embeds or serves them must hold an India Affiliate License, sublicense its end users/deployments, and report usage annually.
technical_features.architecture: SNOMED CT is distributed as release files in the RF2 (Release File Format) package, comprising the International Edition plus national extensions. India-affiliated users download the International Edition, the India Drug Extension (CDCI Terminology Integrated Package), the India AYUSH Extension, the India Geographical Location Extension, the India Patient Instructions Language Extension and India Reference Sets, all through MLDS (mlds.ihtsdotools.org/in). NRCeS additionally publishes the CDCI Flat Files Package as tab-separated text files (Substance, Generic, Brand, Product Name, Supplier, Drug Form and Route-of-Administration masters) that allow systems to standardise drug coding and interoperation without integrating the full terminology, and the Drug Information Service Bundle (DISB), a REST service exposing substance/generic/medicine information. The CDCI extension is modelled on the SNOMED International National Drug Extension model and ISO IDMP-aligned attributes (dose form, route of administration, unit of presentation, strength, supplier, product name).
technical_features.inputs: For Module C, code lookups and mappings: clinical findings, diagnoses, symptoms, procedures, substances, dose forms, routes of administration and medicine concepts. Operationally, the implementation consumes the SNOMED CT International RF2 release files, the CDCI Terminology Integrated Package (or Flat Files TSV) and the ABDM/NRCeS FHIR ValueSets that reference SNOMED codes. It also consumes the Affiliate License identity (MLDS account) and sublicensee register.
technical_features.outputs: Coded data for clinical resources: SNOMED CT concept identifiers in FHIR Coding.system = http://snomed.info/sct, within ABDM OPConsultRecord sections (e.g. problems, procedures, medications) and the CDCI-backed medicine codes for prescriptions. National releases produce RF2 files, the CDCI Flat Files masters (TSV) and DISB API responses. Licensing outputs are a sublicense register and an annual MLDS usage/Declaration of Use report.
technical_features.standards_compliance: Validated, not merely claimed: NRCeS maintains the ABDM FHIR IG and its Medicine Codes ValueSet explicitly names SNOMED CT International Edition and CDCI as the source terminologies; the CDCI concept coverage states it is intended for systems adhering to the MoH&FW-notified Electronic Health Record Standards for India 2016; the extension is modelled on SNOMED International's National Drug Extension model and ISO IDMP-based attributes; and releases are stated to be synchronous with the corresponding SNOMED CT International Edition (the 31 August 2026 CDCI release is synchronous with the August 2026 International Edition). Related Indian standards in the same stack include LOINC via the Common Lab Codes for India (CLCI), ICD-10 via the SNOMED CT to ICD-10 map, and the NAMASTE AYUSH codes as an alternative/complement to the SNOMED CT India AYUSH Extension.
technical_features.offline_capability: Strongly suited to offline/on-device use: because SNOMED CT and CDCI are distributed as downloadable release packages (RF2 files; CDCI TSV flat files plus a terminology-integrated package) and the CDCI Flat Files Package was created precisely to standardise drug coding 'without the need of integrating the complete Terminology', a kiosk can embed a bounded subset locally and resolve codes with no network. The India Patient Instructions Language Extension (Hindi, Marathi, Tamil, Urdu) and the India AYUSH Extension further support offline bilingual rendering. The main operational constraint for the MediKiosk hardware budget is that the full SNOMED CT + CDCI integrated package is large, so the practical approach is to load a curated subset (the ABDM sections actually emitted, plus the medicines encountered) rather than the entire global release into ~4GB-RAM kiosk storage.
technical_features.languages_supported: SNOMED CT is multilingual. India national releases include the India Patient Instructions Language Extension covering Hindi, Marathi, Tamil and Urdu (frequency of dose, route of administration, dose units, dose forms, dosage instructions), and the India AYUSH Extension translates terms into Sanskrit (Ayurveda), Tamil (Siddha) and Urdu (Unani). This directly supports MediKiosk's bilingual (Hindi/English) requirement for patient-facing text and dosage instructions.
technical_features.deployment_model: Deployable on-device, at a clinic LAN/server or in the cloud, provided the Affiliate License and sublicensing conditions are met. NRCeS's stated position is that a SNOMED-enabled application or mobile app (including web-based) that is deployable in India, usable within India, or in a closed network within India is covered by the NRCeS-issued Affiliate License, so a locally-installed or kiosk-embedded terminology store is covered. Deployment outside India, or a web/mobile app with users outside India, requires a separate International Affiliate License from SNOMED International via MLDS. Hardware-wise the terminology can run on CPU-only environments; the constraint is storage and subset selection rather than GPU or model inference.

performance_metrics.accuracy_or_quality_metrics: Not a model, so no F1/ROUGE-type metrics apply. Content quality is managed editorially: NRCeS states each CDCI package is developed through a rigorous authoring and review process and is determined suitable for clinical systems (while cautioning implementers to check suitability for their own environment and to report material errors to nrc-help@cdac.in). The CDCI corpus was contributed by AIIMS New Delhi, 1MG Technologies, C-DAC Noida, RailTel and Pfizer India, with AIIMS Computer Facility performing content review and validation for correctness and completeness.
performance_metrics.latency: Not applicable at the standard level - SNOMED CT is a terminology, so lookup is a local index/table operation whose latency is bounded by the implementation, not the standard. The closest latency-relevant point is that the CDCI Flat Files Package exists specifically to standardise drug coding without integrating the full terminology, which reduces the on-device data volume and lookup cost versus loading the complete SNOMED CT release.
performance_metrics.resource_requirements: No CPU/GPU or model-size requirement. The relevant budget is storage and subset selection: the full SNOMED CT International Edition plus extensions is large (hundreds of megabytes to multiple gigabytes of RF2 content), which is significant for a ~4GB-RAM CPU/iGPU kiosk with no discrete GPU. NRCeS provides a lower-footprint alternative in the CDCI Flat Files Package (TSV masters) and the ABDM workflows only need the sections and medicines actually emitted, so a curated subset is the realistic footprint. The standard itself is CPU-only and offline-capable.
performance_metrics.scale_metrics: CDCI national drug extension content as of the 31 August 2026 release: 3,283 Substances, 10,305 Generic medicines, 93,911 Branded medicines, 72,284 Product (trade/brand) names, 8,213 Suppliers, 423 Drug Forms and 160 Routes of Administration; the extension adds 134 Clinical Drug and 892 Real Clinical Drug concepts and is synchronous with the August 2026 International Edition. The CDCI Flat Files release grew from 15 June 2026 (Substances 3,274; Generic 10,174; Branded 93,019; Product names 71,503; Suppliers 8,121; Drug Forms 422) to 31 August 2026. The government's ABDM Drug Registry (launched 29 June 2026) reports 1.23 lakh+ branded drugs, 10,000+ generic drugs and 29,000+ substances. India affiliate/content scale: India has been a SNOMED International Member since March 2014 and NRCeS publishes the AYUSH Extension, the Geographical Location Extension (7,628 concepts with a simple map to Local Government Directory codes), 30 India Reference Sets, the Patient Instructions Language Extension and the COVID-19 Extension (50 terms).
performance_metrics.evaluation_protocol: Editorial and governance review rather than statistical evaluation: SNOMED International maintains the terminology through its content-development and release process, NRCeS manages the national release process and guidelines, and CDCI concepts are authored and reviewed with AIIMS content validation. There is no published peer-reviewed accuracy benchmark for CDCI because its quality claim is curated breadth and modelling correctness (modelled per SNOMED International Medicinal Product Hierarchy Editorial Guidelines and the SNOMED CT Drug Model for National Extensions v1.0), plus synchronisation with the International Edition.

milestone_significance.relevance_to_module_c: SNOMED CT India and CDCI are the terminology layer under Module C's output contract, and the licensing chain is the thing that can block a commercial kiosk. Module C emits a physician-ready summary against the NRCeS FHIR IG for ABDM (OPConsultRecord), whose sections and medicine ValueSets are SNOMED-based; the ABDM Medicine Codes ValueSet is explicitly SNOMED CT International plus CDCI, and MedicationRequest requires CDCI when branded Indian medicines are coded. So Module C cannot be genuinely ABDM-conformant for medication or clinical findings without using these code systems - which means the product must hold an India Affiliate License, sublicense its deployed kiosks/hospital instances as end users, and file an annual usage report, even though the content is free in-country. Two secondary relevance points: the India Patient Instructions Language Extension supplies Hindi/Marathi/Tamil/Urdu dosage-instruction synonyms that Module C can use for the patient-language rendering, and the India AYUSH Extension (plus NAMASTE) is the available SNOMED route for Prakriti/Vikriti-adjacent AYUSH terminology that OPConsultRecord does not natively section. The licensing resolution is favourable: not a blocker, but a mandatory process step (MLDS registration + sublicense flow + reporting) before shipping.
milestone_significance.what_to_adopt_or_reject: Adopt: (1) SNOMED CT as the coding system for clinical findings/procedures and CDCI for Indian medicines, because it is what ABDM ValueSets actually use and it strengthens the NRCeS-conformance and India-residency story; (2) an early MLDS Affiliate License registration (NRCeS gives a 4-5 business day download turnaround) and a maintained sublicensee register, treating sublicensing and the 15 January annual Declaration of Use as product-release checklist items; (3) a curated, offline-embeddable subset (only the ABDM sections emitted plus encountered medicines, or the CDCI Flat Files/TSV route) to respect the ~4GB kiosk budget and avoid loading the full global release; (4) the India Patient Instructions Language Extension for bilingual dosage text, and evaluate the India AYUSH Extension for any AYUSH-coded fields. Reject or guard against: (a) embedding SNOMED/CDCI code content without an Affiliate License on the assumption that 'it is free in India' - free is not the same as unlicensed; (b) shipping a build that lets a hospital or user deploy the app outside India without an International Affiliate License, since the NRCeS licence covers only India-deployable/India-usable/India-closed-network use; (c) redistributing or re-serving the terminology in a way that breaches the Affiliate License or, for the Flat Files Package, its bundled License.txt; (d) silently bundling the full terminology when a subset would both comply and fit; (e) assuming the CDCI Flat Files Package and the CDCI Terminology Integrated Package carry identical terms - the integrated package is under the SNOMED CT Affiliate License, while the Flat Files Package is under its own License.txt.
milestone_significance.limitations_and_risks: Named limitations and residual uncertainty: (1) The exact text of the CDCI Flat Files Package bundled License.txt was not retrievable from the public web (it ships inside the package), so its precise redistribution/embedding terms are unverified - the safe assumption is that it is a separate, NRCeS-specific licence that must be read before embedding, and not a permissive open licence. (2) The full SNOMED CT + CDCI integrated package is large relative to the kiosk's ~4GB-RAM, CPU/iGPU budget, so subsetting is a real engineering constraint, not optional. (3) Coverage gaps: CDCI covers NLEM 2015 & 2022, Jan Aushadhi, AMRIT, Telemedicine Practice Guidelines, HIV and COVID-19 lists but explicitly excludes devices, surgical implants and combi packs, and the extension currently models single-ingredient and up-to-five-ingredient clinical drugs but not Packaged Clinical Drug / Real Packaged Clinical Drug concepts (flagged as possible future work) - so some prescribed items may not have a CDCI code. (4) AYUSH terminology is split between the SNOMED CT India AYUSH Extension and the Ministry of AYUSH NAMASTE portal, and OPConsultRecord has no dedicated AYUSH sections, so mapping AYUSH findings into the summary remains non-trivial. (5) Licensing process risk, not cost risk: failure to keep the annual usage report current deactivates the MLDS account and cuts off access to the terminology and national extensions, which would break a released product's code validation. (6) The terminology is versioned (biannual International releases; frequent CDCI releases), so conformance to a ValueSet/expansion is tied to a release date and must be pinned and re-validated. (7) SNOMED CT usage in non-Member territories and web-application modes may attract special permission and fees - relevant if the product ever exposes terminology outside India.
milestone_significance.differentiator_vs_medikiosk: SNOMED CT India and CDCI strengthen rather than erode MediKiosk's differentiation, because they are the coded substrate the NRCeS-conformant emission claim depends on. MediKiosk's stated differentiators line up with the standard: offline-first works because SNOMED/CDCI ship as downloadable releases and the CDCI Flat Files Package exists specifically to standardise drug coding without integrating the full terminology; India residency is inherent (NRCeS national releases, India-only Affiliate License coverage); NRCeS-conformant emission is only credible if the emitted OPConsultRecord actually uses the SNOMED codes and the CDCI-backed medicine ValueSet; per-field provenance is easier to defend when each coded finding carries a SNOMED concept id and release version; and physician attestation fits the completeness/accuracy duty that applies when coded data is used for decisions or shared. The one place MediKiosk must match, not just adopt, is AYUSH terminology: OPConsultRecord has no native AYUSH sections, so MediKiosk must decide between the SNOMED CT India AYUSH Extension and NAMASTE for Prakriti/Vikriti-style content and document the mapping. The differentiator is therefore not the terminology itself (it is a shared standard) but the discipline of subsetting it to the kiosk budget, pinning the release version, sublicensing deployments and reporting annually - a compliance/adherence advantage over cloud intake products that cite SNOMED without holding a valid Affiliate License.

business_info.license: SNOMED CT is proprietary IP owned by SNOMED International and is not offered under an open-source licence. India licenses are Affiliate Licenses issued under the Affiliate License Agreement: registering at MLDS, accepting the agreement, and receiving download access. Use within India is free because India is a Member country and SNOMED International does not charge Affiliate Licensees for use in Member countries (MoH&FW has made SNOMED CT freely available for all use within India). Vendor obligations under the Affiliate License: sublicense the end users who use the SNOMED-enabled software/service (each system deployment requires a sub-licence), maintain a register of sublicensees, and submit an annual usage report/Declaration of Use via MLDS (due 15 January). The CDCI Terminology Integrated Package is available to Affiliate Licensees through MLDS and is 'available for use under terms provided in SNOMED CT Affiliate License'; the CDCI Flat Files Package (and the DISB) are 'available for use under terms provided in the License.txt file included in the Package'. Use outside India, or a web/mobile application with users outside India, requires a separate International Affiliate License from SNOMED International via MLDS, and web-application/browser deployment modes may require special permission and fees.
business_info.pricing: Zero for use within India under the India Affiliate License (content and national releases free). Costs are administrative: an MLDS account, sublicense management and annual reporting. For use in non-Member countries, Affiliate License fees are charged annually and are based on the country's World Bank Territory Band; an International Affiliate License is required and separate licences are needed for each Member country in which the product is used, deployed or distributed.
business_info.funding: Not applicable in a venture sense - SNOMED CT is funded through SNOMED International membership subscriptions (India pays a national-wealth-based member fee that gives it a General Assembly seat) and NRCeS is a government programme of MoH&FW at C-DAC Pune. CDCI development is government-funded with contributed corpora from AIIMS New Delhi, 1MG, C-DAC Noida, RailTel and Pfizer India.
business_info.commercial_status: Government programme / freely available national standard within India. India has been a SNOMED International Member since March 2014; NRCeS is the National Release Centre. There is no per-seat charge to Indian users, but compliance with the Affiliate License, sublicensing and annual reporting is mandatory and enforceable (account deactivation on non-reporting).

competition_ecosystem.competitors: Alternative or overlapping clinical terminologies/code systems for the same slots: ICD-11/ICD-10 (WHO classification, via the SNOMED CT to ICD-10 map or directly), LOINC (via the Common Lab Codes for India for lab tests), the Ministry of AYUSH NAMASTE codes and the SNOMED CT India AYUSH Extension for Ayurveda/Siddha/Unani, openEHR archetypes and NHS/other national terminology subsets, and generic drug code catalogues (e.g. commercial drug databases). Within the ABDM output contract, SNOMED CT + CDCI is the mainstream/expected choice rather than one option among equals, because the NRCeS ValueSets are built on them; NAMASTE is the main complementary system for AYUSH content that SNOMED does not section.
competition_ecosystem.integrations: ABDM: the NRCeS FHIR IG for ABDM uses SNOMED CT for clinical codes and the CDCI-backed Medicine Codes ValueSet for medications, and the Drug Registry (launched 29 June 2026, built with CDSCO + NRCeS) uses SNOMED CT to standardise Indian drug data across digital health systems. Distribution/licensing: MLDS. Tooling: NRCeS publishes the Drug Information Service Bundle (DISB) REST services for substances/generics/branded medicines, and C-DAC offers the CSNOtk toolkit for SNOMED CT integration. Related NRCeS national releases that co-deploy with CDCI include the India Reference Sets, the Geographic Location Extension (LGD-mapped), the Patient Instructions Language Extension and the AYUSH Extension. ICD-10 mapping is distributed as part of the SNOMED International release package.
competition_ecosystem.ecosystem_notes: The ecosystem direction is strongly favourable and consolidating on SNOMED CT + CDCI for Indian medication and clinical coding: NRCeS keeps releasing CDCI on a near-quarterly cadence through 2026; the Ministry of Health launched a national Drug Registry under ABDM in June 2026 explicitly using SNOMED CT; and the ABDM FHIR IG ValueSets already bind to SNOMED/CDCI. For MediKiosk this is a procurement and conformance tailwind - ABDM-aligned tenders and NRCeS validation increasingly assume these code systems. The main ecosystem frictions are licensing process discipline (Affiliate License, sublicensing, annual reporting), terminology versioning (pin the release), the AYUSH terminology split between SNOMED AYUSH Extension and NAMASTE, and the size of the terminology relative to constrained kiosk hardware.

history.release_date: SNOMED CT itself dates from the 1999-2002 merger of SNOMED RT and the UK Clinical Terms (Read Codes) and is maintained by SNOMED International. India became a SNOMED International Member in March 2014, with NRCeS at C-DAC Pune designated as the National Release Centre. CDCI (the India national drug extension, also called the India Drug Extension for SNOMED CT) is maintained by NRCeS with recurring releases.
history.key_milestones: 1999-2002 - SNOMED CT formed and SNOMED International established. March 2014 - India joins SNOMED International as a Member; MoH&FW designates C-DAC Pune / NRCeS as the NRC. 2016 - MoH&FW-notified Electronic Health Record Standards for India 2016 (the adherence reference for CDCI). 2018-2021 - NRCeS publishes India extension/reference-set release notes (reference sets 2021, geographical location and patient-instructions language extensions 2021, COVID-19 extension 2021). 2020-2021 - ABDM/NDHM FHIR IG establishes SNOMED + CDCI medicine ValueSets. 2023 - SNOMED CT Affiliate License Agreement (2023) in use for India licensing. 2025 - CDCI Flat Files Package releases (e.g. 15 July 2024 and 20 June 2025) and continued expansion of brand coverage. 2026 - CDCI Flat Files releases on 15 June 2026 and 31 August 2026, synchronous CDCI Terminology Integrated Package release, and the national Drug Registry launch.
history.recent_changes_last_6_months: Within roughly March-September 2026: (1) NRCeS published a CDCI release on 15 June 2026 (Flat Files Package), then the current release on 31 August 2026 (Substances 3,283; Generic 10,305; Branded 93,911; Product names 72,284; Suppliers 8,213; Drug Forms 423; Route 160) together with the synchronous CDCI Terminology Integrated Package (India Drug Extension) release. (2) The India Drug Extension release note records that the extension added 134 Clinical Drug and 892 Real Clinical Drug concepts and is synchronous with the August 2026 SNOMED CT International Edition, modelled per SNOMED International Medicinal Product Hierarchy Editorial Guidelines and the National Drug Extension model, with OWL Expression and Concrete Value Relationship files. (3) On 29 June 2026 the Union Health Minister launched the national Drug Registry under ABDM, developed with CDSCO and NRCeS using SNOMED CT, reported to contain 1.23 lakh+ branded drugs, 10,000+ generic drugs and 29,000+ substances. (4) The India AYUSH Extension and Common Lab Codes for India (CLCI) releases were current as of 29 June 2026, and NRCeS's site shows the national releases page updated through 2026. (5) The SNOMED CT Affiliate License, sublicensing and annual-usage-reporting obligations (declaration due 15 January in MLDS) remained the operative licensing mechanics for India.

market_positioning.target_users: Health IT implementers, EHR/HIS vendors, health apps and kiosks, hospitals and clinics, laboratories, pharmacies and supply-chain systems that need standardised clinical and drug coding; SNOMED International Affiliates (developers/distributors); and national programmes. For MediKiosk specifically, the consumers are Module C's FHIR emitter (codes) and the hospital's ABDM-compliant stack.
market_positioning.market_segment: Clinical terminology / semantic interoperability standards, and specifically Indian medication coding (CDCI) inside the ABDM FHIR tooling segment. It is the terminology layer underneath intake, summary, prescribing and interoperability products rather than a competing intake or scribing product.
market_positioning.positioning_statement: NRCeS positions SNOMED CT as 'the most comprehensive, multilingual clinical healthcare terminology in the world', clinically validated and semantically rich, made freely available for all use within India with NRCeS acting as the single point of contact for EHR standards adoption; CDCI is positioned as the common drug codes that let Indian clinical, reporting, stock and supply-chain systems use the same codes and interoperate reliably under the ABDM/ABHA digital-health ecosystem, with releases available to Affiliate Licensees via MLDS.
